title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: container and gross-weight limits per acceptance
content:
## What this card covers
This card gives, for every acceptance category of the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product, the maximum number of containers under one acceptance, the maximum dangerous-goods gross weight per container and the maximum dangerous-goods gross weight under one acceptance.

## Limits by category
| Category | Containers per acceptance, at most | Gross weight per container, at most (kg) | Gross weight per acceptance, at most (kg) |
|---|---|---|---|
| AHL DG Limited Quantity | 10 | 24000 | 120000 |
| AHL DG Class 9 Standard | 10 | 26000 | 160000 |
| AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives | 8 | 24000 | 120000 |
| AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers | 5 | 22000 | 80000 |
| AHL DG Compressed Gases | 5 | 20000 | 60000 |
| AHL DG Special Approval | 2 | 18000 | 20000 |

Each figure is a ceiling: a value equal to the figure is within the limit.

## Comparing the three limits (worked from the table)
For every category, the container limit multiplied by the per-container weight limit exceeds the per-acceptance weight limit. Taking AHL DG Special Approval: two containers at 18000 kg each would total 36000 kg, which is above the 20000 kg ceiling for the acceptance. Taking AHL DG Toxics and Oxidizers: five containers at 22000 kg each would total 110000 kg, above the 80000 kg ceiling. Neither weight limit can therefore be read as implied by the other; each is a separate ceiling.

## Basis Q&A
- *Which category allows the heaviest container?* AHL DG Class 9 Standard, at 26000 kg per container.
- *Which categories share the same three limits?* None share all three; AHL DG Limited Quantity and AHL DG Flammables and Corrosives share both weight ceilings but differ in containers per acceptance (10 against 8).
